children: A nationwide ground stop and a widespread Microsoft

outage disrupted travel and work Friday, exposing vulnerabilities in essential infrastructure. Authorities and Microsoft attributed the incidents to technology upgrades and reported no evidence of malicious activity, the Associated Press reported.

For investors, the disruptions underscore potential costs from service interruptions and reputational damage, while highlighting demand for infrastructure modernization. The financial consequences remain unclear.

The aviation shutdown lasted more than four hours after an upgrade overwhelmed aging air traffic equipment, administration officials said. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy linked the failure to work by L3Harris Technologies
at a remote site and a router issue. L3Harris
the FAA’s investigation and has completed roughly 70% of a planned communications transition from copper wiring to fiber optics.
Flights were recovering Saturday, with normal schedules expected by late Sunday. Congress has approved $12.5 billion for air traffic modernization, and the White House is seeking another $30 billion.
Microsoft said services were fully restored Saturday after a network change exposed a problem originating in an earlier capacity upgrade.

title: Microsoft outage, flight disruptions expose infrastructure risks
